summary: This resolution expels Representative Cory Mills from the House under Article I, Section 5 of the Constitution based on allegations of domestic assault, threats and harassment of a former partner, federal contracting conflicts of interest, and false claims about his military record.

scores.thoughts: The resolution concerns the expulsion of a House member for alleged misconduct and ethical violations. It contains no provisions, findings, or directives related to federal spending levels, appropriations, or budget policy.
The resolution addresses expulsion based on personal conduct and conflicts of interest. It has no provisions affecting tax rates, tax policy, or revenue measures.
The bill is strictly about removing a member from Congress and makes no reference to healthcare systems, coverage, or regulation.
No content in the resolution relates to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
The resolution does not address immigration policy, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions or findings in the bill concern reproductive rights or abortion access.

While the preamble references the member's defense contracting businesses and military record, the operative text is solely about expulsion and does not alter defense spending, procurement policy, or military budgets.
The resolution has no connection to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No elements of the bill relate to welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
The bill does not engage with education funding, school choice, or federal education policy.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy appear in the resolution.

The preamble details allegations of assault and an injunction, but the bill itself is a congressional expulsion measure under Article I, Section 5 and does not reform criminal sentencing, policing, or justice policy.
The resolution contains no provisions on tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No content addresses deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
The bill does not address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
Although the preamble notes the member's companies operating in foreign countries, the resolution does not change foreign aid levels or policy.
The resolution has no bearing on voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
Allegations mention threats involving intimate videos, but the bill itself is an expulsion resolution and does not establish or alter technology or privacy regulations.
No provisions relate to worker protections, union rights, or labor policy.
The resolution does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
